title: Make the URN name segment match the file's basename

facts.note: Requires parsing the file for a URN and checking it has six segments; applies to existing files as well as new or edited ones, with no change, phase or finding precondition.

values: basename not in the exempt structural-role set
facts.note: Exempt basenames: composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware.

fires: A file carries a six-segment URN whose name segment names a different component than the file's basename (e.g. a header copied from a sibling file).
An existing file, not touched in the current change, carries a six-segment URN whose name segment does not match its non-exempt basename after normalisation.
doesNotFire: The name segment differs from the basename only by case or non-alphanumerics (e.g. `order-row.ts` with `OrderRow`).
The file's basename is an exempt structural role.
The URN is not six segments (the check is skipped).

given: A file carries a six-segment URN and its basename is not an exempt structural role
when: the file's URN and basename are compared
then: The URN `{Name}` segment (segment 3) MUST identify the component the file implements and match the file's basename, compared case- and separator-insensitively.
prefer: During GREEN: derive the name from the actual file/component being implemented.
During GREEN: correct a copied or stale header before considering a file rename.
During GREEN: keep structural-role filenames as structural roles when that is their real responsibility.
avoid: Copy-pasting a URN header without updating its name segment.
Renaming a correctly named component merely to preserve a wrong URN.
Using an exempt structural name to evade component identity.
unless: The basename is a structural role (composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware): the file assembles rather than implements.
The URN is not six segments: skipped.
why: A URN naming a different component than its file is worse than a missing one: it binds the file's evidence to somebody else's component, so both are wrong and neither is obviously wrong.
evidence: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-URN-004 / BUN-GREEN-URN-NAME-MATCHES-001 finding.
The URN name and implementation identity agree.
verifier_detail: Name segment = segment 3 of the URN, identifying the component the file implements.
Normalise both the name segment and the file basename to lowercase alphanumerics (ignore case and all non-alphanumerics) before comparing; `order-row.ts` matches `OrderRow`.

Exempt structural basenames: composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware. This is the Vite exempt set plus the Bun stack idioms `server`, `routes`, `layout`, `partial`, `fragment`, `middleware`, because a full-stack Bun app's entrypoint is `server.ts` and its htmx fragments are named for their role, not for a component.
URNs that are not six segments are skipped.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Source name: 'The URN name segment matches the filename'.
Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized by validator `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-URN-004).
Source terms: name_segment; structural_role_name ('a filename naming a ROLE rather than a component — index, server, routes, layout, partial, composition, wagon'; full exempt list is in exceptions).
Summary framing: a 'the URN names this file' obligation.
Source note: a mismatched name is the failure a copy-pasted header produces, which is how it usually arises.
